title: Traffic safety heuristics and split design notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note collection of heuristics, guardrails, and pragmatic split-design patterns for cross-functional rollouts (canaries and A/Bs) for LLM-powered product surfaces. The goal is to provide operationally lightweight, reproducible patterns that product, SRE, serving-runtime, and CS teams can use as a baseline when shipping feature flags, model swaps, or routing policies.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Use a 3-stage exposure ramp: internal -> small external cohort (0.5–2%) -> progressive scaling tied to objective metrics and budget SLOs.
- Maintain independent safety/quality SLOs (latency P95, error %, hallucination/NG-rate on eval prompts) and cost SLOs (tokens per response, p99 cost spike).
- Automate soft rollback triggers but require human confirm for irreversible actions (full model switch; infra migration).

Safety heuristics matrix (practical rules):
- Latency gating: if P95 increases by >=30% relative to baseline and absolute P95 > SLO, freeze exposure and alert SRE + product.
- Error gating: 5xx rate or inference failures > 0.5% absolute increase on the canary slice -> pause and investigate.
- Quality gating: for text features, run a small seeded eval set on live traffic (synthetic prompts + golden responses). If quality delta (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity/LLM-eval score) drops > 7% on canary, stop ramp.
- Hallucination/unsafe output heuristic: monitor model-safety classifier score + user reports. If classifier-flagged outputs > 0.2% AND user-reported incidents spike, revert.
- Cost gating: per-request median token consumption increases by >20% or token-per-minute spend breaches budget window -> throttle.

Traffic split strategies (pattern recipes):
1) Random uniform small-slice canary (fast, low overhead)
   - Use for purely model-variant changes where no stateful routing is required.
   - Start at 0.5% for 24h (min 2k requests) -> 1% for 24h -> 5% if all gates pass.

2) Cohort-driven canary (user/tenant based)
   - Use for large customers or private deployments (Dedicated/Private).
   - Create cohort list (alpha customers) and route by tenant id. Ensure data residency and logging controls.

3) Query-intent orthogonalization (route by inferred intent)
   - Useful for features that only affect certain intents (e.g., summarization). Only expose to traffic with matching intent predictions.

4) Hybrid time-window + cohort split (for cost spikes)
   - Route limited heavier models to low-load windows for a given cohort to limit cost and risk.

Staging cadence and stoplight criteria (recipe):
- Pre-launch (canary build): internal dogfood + smoke tests, SLA checks, eval-suite run.
- Stage A (0.5% random): run for 24h. Must satisfy: latency gates, error gates, seeded-eval pass, no critical user reports.
- Stage B (1–5%): run 48–72h depending on volume. Monitor business metrics (CTR, downstream conversion) and cost.
- Stage C (progressive): scale with 2x steps (5 -> 10 -> 25 -> 50) daily only if all gates green; require product + SRE signoff >10%.

Metrics and signals (what we actually watch):
- Core infra: P50/P95/P99 inference latency, CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth, request rate.
- Reliability: 5xx rate, timeout rate, KV-cache-miss trend (for cached routes), memory OOMs.
- Cost: tokens per response (median/p90), peak-token-rate (tokens/sec), per-route spend rate.
- Quality: seeded-eval pass rate (binary pass/fail threshold), embedding-similarity delta to baseline, top-n rerank accuracy for ranking surfaces.
- User-observed: NPS-like “bad response” flags, support tickets tagged by CS.

Observability implementation notes (practical):
- Create a dedicated canary dashboard per experiment that overlays baseline vs canary slices for the selected metrics.
- Keep retention short for canary dashboards (48–72h) to reduce alert noise.
- Add a synthetic probe job that sends the seeded-eval set every 15m and posts summary to Slack channel with pass/fail counts.

Automatic rollback and recovery patterns:
- Soft rollback (automated): triggered by threshold breaches (latency or error). Action = route traffic off variant to baseline + create incident ticket automatically. No infra changes.
- Hard rollback (manual): severe quality regressions or data exposure. Action = rollback + postmortem + 24h freeze window for same model family. Requires product sign-off.
- Circuit-breaker: global rate limiter that can be tripped when total token spend or request error rate exceeds emergency threshold; SRE pager if tripped.

Inter-team runbook bits (who does what):
- Product: defines target metrics, business guardrails, acceptance criteria for metrics important to the feature.
- SRE/Infra: configures routing rules, implements circuit-breaker thresholds, sets up canary infra, owns rollout automation.
- Serving/Applied ML: provides seeded-eval suite, inspects model failures, ships model variants and quantization notes.
- Devex/Docs: publishes experiment runbook and one-click rollback playbook to the shared console.
- CS/Support: prepped with FAQs, canary-customer list, and a 1-click revert toggle in the console for dedicated tenants.

Experiment design considerations for LLM-specific changes:
- Cold-cache vs warm-cache: model swaps can change KV cache hit profiles. Include a cache-warmup period and compare cache-hit rate on canary vs baseline.
- Context-length effects: for long-context models, add a synthetic long-context subset to seeded-eval to detect pathological latency or memory blowups.
- Quantized vs full-precision variants: benchmark both on same sample of live traffic before ramping. Watch for increased hallucinations with aggressive quantization.
- Fallback policies: always configure a lighter-weight model variant as an automatic fallback (e.g., smaller quantized model) for latency/timeouts.

Edge cases and private deployment notes (Dedicated/Private):
- For Private deployments, customers sometimes want local rollouts; provide a minimal checklist for offline verification (local smoke script, local seeded-eval results exported).
- Audit log policy: ensure canary switching events are recorded with requester, timestamp, and revert action. Required for compliance.
- Network egress: when routing to a new model variant that calls external tool integrations, flag during gating for potential egress policy violations.

Communication and incident flow:
- Slack channels: #rollouts-prod (read-only for alerts), #rollouts-ops (muted unless oncall), and a one-off experiment channel created per rollout (archive after completion).
- Pager thresholds: SRE configures pagers for infra-level thresholds only; product and applied-ml get startup messages but are paged after 15m if unresolved.

Open questions / TODOs (actionable items):
- Decide standard seeded-eval size for live tests (current suggestion: 300 prompts including 50 edge/long-context).
- Simulate behavior for tenant-cohort ramp for low-volume customers (how many requests needed to reach statistical confidence?).
- Add a standard template for the canary dashboard (widgets + alert thresholds) and check into GitHub.

Appendix: quick checklist before flipping flag
- [ ] seeded-eval local pass (serving-team)
- [ ] infra smoke tests (SRE)
- [ ] circuit-breaker configured and tested (SRE)
- [ ] customer/tenant whitelist loaded if cohort test (CS)
- [ ] support playbook + canned responses ready (CS)
- [ ] cost budget window configured (finance/ops)
- [ ] oncall rotation notified and channel created (product)

Notes to self:
- This is intentionally light-weight; aim for low-friction experiments so teams actually use it. Complex risky migrations (infra, stateful routing) should be handled as formal releases not quick canaries.
- Keep iterating on the seeded-eval — the most useful signal so far has been small, targeted prompt sets reflecting common user failure modes.

Unresolved questions for next sync:
- What's the default freeze window after an automated soft-rollback? (suggest 4h active freeze + 24h review)
- Should we enable automatic tenant notification on rollback or leave that manual?
- How to standardize telemetry across Dedicated/Private vs Hosted to make gates comparable?

End of notes.
